Class PnmlModelGenerator

java.lang.Object
ua.stetsenkoinna.pnml.PnmlModelGenerator
public class PnmlModelGenerator extends Object
Writes a composed GraphPetriObjModel as a PNML document.

The composition is expressed with the structuring PNML already has: one <page> per Petri-object inside a single <net>, and, this is the part that makes the document mean the same thing to a reader that is not this tool, one <referencePlace> or <referenceTransition> per link. A reference node is how ISO/IEC 15909-2 says "this node is shared with another page"; without them the pages are unrelated nets and every link is invisible, however faithfully a tool-specific block records it.

How each kind of link is drawn

Uniformly: the reference node lives on the source object's page and stands for the target element.

  • Place fusion A.p = B.q, page A's <place> is replaced by <referencePlace id="A.p" ref="B.q"/>. The replacement, rather than an addition, is what keeps the page's place ordinals unchanged, and it is the right way round because wiring a fusion redirects the source object's slot to the target's instance: the target's place is the one that survives. Every arc of page A that touched the place keeps pointing at the same id.
  • Transition to place A.t -> B.p, page A gains a stand-in <referencePlace> for B.p and an ordinary arc into it.

There is no third kind. A place of one object feeding a transition of another is written as a shared place plus an ordinary arc inside the object that owns the transition, which says the same thing without giving a transition a second set of input places.

How the hierarchy is drawn

An object nested inside another has its <page> written inside that object's page, which is how ISO/IEC 15909-2 states a page hierarchy. Only top-level objects, and the page holding the elements that belong to no object, sit directly under <net>. See nestPages(ua.stetsenkoinna.graphnet.GraphPetriObjModel, java.util.List<org.w3c.dom.Element>): nothing tool-specific is written about the hierarchy at all.

What still has to be tool-specific

Only what a P/T net cannot say: an informational (test) arc inside an object's own net, which has no P/T form at all; the object's priority, position and template; whether a reference node is the object's own slot or a stand-in, a difference flattening deliberately erases; and the marking of a place that ceases to exist on flattening.

The <petriObjectLinks> block is still written and is now redundant with the structure. It earns its place as compatibility, a reader that predates reference nodes recovers the arc-like links from it in full, and as a record of what the user declared, addressed by element id rather than by position alone. It is not a second source of truth, and readers here treat it as subordinate.
